brief: NDX and SMH are breaking key technical levels (NDX below its trend line and 100-day MA, next support the 200-day MA; SMH below its formation near $544) as hedge funds have aggressively rebuilt tech longs: GS prime brokerage shows HFs bought US TMT in 10 of 11 sessions, the two-week pace in the 97th percentile of five years. That rebuild matters because dispersion is extreme (TMT winners-vs-losers vol around 76 versus 13 for SPX), leaving rebuilt longs vulnerable to AI and Iran headlines even as broad-index fear stayed low, the Panic Index posting its third-largest one-day drop in three years. Weekend catalysts: Amodei's call to pace the frontier hit Asian AI stocks, SoftBank down double digits, raising capex-durability worries, though Privorotsky expects tighter safety gates rather than a spending stop since Microsoft, Meta and China are not leaving the race. Bigger concern is energy: Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, moving 4-5mb/d, remains shut, Yanbu inventories cover exports five to seven more days, and around 4% of global supply is at risk if the outage persists, plus a Houthi push toward Bab el-Mandeb and a postponed Iran-Gulf meeting. AI is a valuation scare, energy a compounding risk, VIX still looks too low.
